newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia presidential campaign adviser convicted.
newsitem.headline: Colombia presidential campaign adviser convicted.

text.p: One of President Ernesto Samper's former election campaign team members was sentenced to six-and-a-half years jail on Thursday on charges of receiving donations from drug traffickers, court sources said.

Juan Manuel Avella, the administrative director of the president's 1994 election campaign, has been in custody for almost two years in connection with the drug-financing scandal that has dogged most of Samper's administration.

Avella, a member of the ruling Liberal party, was found guilty on Thursday of illicit enrichment and handling false documents by a regional judge in Bogota, a court spokesman said. He had always maintained his innocence.
Even before Samper took office it was alleged his campaign received more than $6 million in donations from the Cali drug cartel -- responsible for an estimated 80 percent of the world cocaine supply.

Samper himself was cleared of any wrongdoing after an extensive investigation in Congress, dominated by his own Liberal Party. U.S. anti-drug authorities, however, doubt Samper's claims that he knew nothing of the drug funding and still accuse him of being a "truly corrupt president."
One of the other main figures in the campaign, its general manager Fernando Botero, is currently serving a seven-and-half year term for his part in the funding scandal.

Botero was arrested in mid-1995 and is expected to be freed on parole in the next few days after his sentence was slashed for cooperating with justice officials and was granted time off for good behaviour, local media reported.
